euronews.title: Venezuela earthquake damages add up to almost $20 billion, World Bank says
euronews.description: Almost a month after the devastating earthquakes, Venezuela has a mammoth task ahead in terms of rebuilding, rehabilitating and mitigating the social and economic damage of the biggest natural disaster in decades.

euronews.description: People taking GLP-1 drugs have a low risk of hair loss, which is significantly higher than for those on other diabetes medications, a new study has found.

euronews.description: A wildfire spreads near Le Porge in Gironde, France, as firefighters battle flames across the forest and thousands of people are evacuated.

euronews.description: A massive fire in Norway has destroyed more than 100 homes and forced hundreds of people to evacuate. As the blaze spread, posts on social media began linking it to claims that Oslo had banned imports of Israeli settlement products. The Cube investigates.

rfi.description: A wildfire near Bordeaux in south-west France has led to the evacuation of a further 7,000 people on Thursday, bringing the total number of tourists and residents moved to 12,000, local authorities said.

rfi.title: Germany approves factory use for controversial French-Russian nuclear project
rfi.description: German authorities on Wednesday gave the green light to a controversial French-Russian nuclear project which will use a factory based in Germany for production, and which critics fear will enable spying and sabotage by Moscow.

rfi.title: Zizou's back: Zinedine Zidane set to take charge of Les Bleus
rfi.description: The French Football Federation will hold a news conference on 28 July to unveil the next coach of the national team, the governing body said on Thursday. Former star player Zinedine Zidane has long been viewed as the leading candidate for the role.

rfi.title: DRC's Ebola outbreak kills more than 1,000, with children hit hardest
rfi.description: More than 1,030 people have died from an Ebola outbreak declared in May in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda, the World Health Organization said on Wednesday, as confirmed cases in the DRC surpassed 2,530, according to government data.

rfi.title: United States announces landmark civilian nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia
rfi.description: The United States on Wednesday announced a deal with Saudi Arabia that would establish a civilian nuclear programme in the Gulf country, with Washington insisting the agreement includes nonproliferation safeguards.

rfi.title: Macron talks environment minister out of quitting over pesticide U-turn
rfi.description: France's environment minister, Monique Barbut, will remain in her post, given the "urgency" to act on climate change, after submitting her resignation to President Emmanuel Macron over a bill to reintroduce bee-harming pesticides, her team said Wednesday.

rfi.title: French model recruiter with links to Epstein found dead near Paris

rfi.title: France approves social media ban for children under 15, in EU first

rfi.title: Gabon and France deepen industrial cooperation with Eramet manganese deal
rfi.description: French mining group Eramet is considering a major expansion of manganese processing in Gabon under an agreement that could strengthen the country’s industrial base, modernise its railway network and reduce its reliance on exports of unprocessed ore.

rfi.title: Germany looks to Azerbaijan as Armenia ties shift regional relationships
rfi.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev have signed a series of economic agreements aimed at deepening Berlin's access to Baku's gas reserves and transit routes. The deal comes as Germany works to diversify its energy supply, and as Azerbaijan balances a Europe-leaning Armenia against a recently repaired relationship with Moscow.

rfi.title: France’s emergency agriculture bill passed, amid divisions over pesticides
rfi.description: France’s National Assembly has approved an emergency agriculture bill after a tense overnight debate, clearing the way for the possible temporary return of two pesticides banned in the country but still authorised elsewhere in the European Union.

rfi.title: France and Germany move to tackle EU’s growing trade deficit with China
rfi.description: France and Germany are pressing for a stronger European Union response to China’s growing trade surplus and industrial overcapacity, as concerns mount over the impact on key European sectors.

rfi.title: Ukraine’s wartime unity put to the test by protests over military leadership
rfi.description: Protests over the dismissal of Ukraine’s reformist defence minister entered a fifth day on Monday, deepening a political crisis that has placed President Volodymyr Zelensky under mounting pressure to overhaul the country’s military leadership.

rfi.title: Countdown to the ballot: Zambia gears up for August elections
rfi.description: This week on Spotlight on Africa, we're heading to Zambia, where general elections are set to take place on the 13th August. Voters will go to the polls to elect a president, members of the National Assembly, councillors and council chairs. Incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema has already picked up endorsements from within his own camp, the UPND Alliance, the coalition that's held power since 2021. So what's at stake, and who's in the running?

rfi.title: Senegal's Faye backs former president Sall's bid for UN top job in U-turn
rfi.description: Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye has endorsed former president Macky Sall's candidacy to become the next United Nations secretary-general, the foreign ministry said on Monday, giving his predecessor crucial backing from his home country despite deep political divisions.

rfi.title: Burnham becomes UK's seventh PM in a decade after Starmer resigns
rfi.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said politicians “need to be better” as he delivered his first speech on Monday as the United Kingdom's new leader.

rfi.title: France's Fontainebleau forest faces long recovery after wildfires
rfi.description: The wildfires that ravaged more than 2,000 hectares of the Fontainebleau Forest have destroyed habitats and have put its diversity of plant and animal life under threat.

rfi.title: France welcomes Gabon's Oligui as mineral and military ties defy African rift
rfi.description: Gabon's President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema begins a three-day official visit to France on Monday, underlining the close relationship between Paris and one of its few remaining key allies in Francophone Africa.

lemonde.description: Le feu en Gironde, qualifié d’exceptionnellement intense par les pompiers, a vu sa surface multipliée par six en moins de trois heures et progresse vers Arès et Lège-Cap-Ferret. Dans le Var, le feu qui a parcouru 2 500 hectares n’était toujours pas fixé.

lemonde.title: Une épidémie de rougeole « hors de contrôle » aux Etats-Unis, sur fond de vaccino-scepticisme d’une partie des habitants et de l’administration Trump

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre au Moyen-Orient : l’Iran revendique des bombardements sur des sites militaires américains en Jordanie et au Koweït
lemonde.description: Alors que l’armée américaine a dit avoir procédé à une « nouvelle série de frappes contre l’Iran pour la 12ᵉ nuit d’affilée », Téhéran affirme avoir détruit un radar américain du système antimissile Thaad en Jordanie. Au Koweït, l’armée iranienne dit avoir visé notamment des dépôts de munitions et des réservoirs de carburant.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : des morts dans des bombardements ukrainiens en Russie et en Crimée ; Moscou poursuit ses attaques contre des installations énergétiques
lemonde.description: Une personne est morte dans la région russe de Belgorod, près de la frontière avec l’Ukraine, dans une attaque de drone ukrainienne dans la nuit de mercredi à jeudi. En Crimée, péninsule annexée en 2014 par la Russie, une personne a aussi été tuée.

lemonde.description: « Sois belle et produis » (4/6). Attributs féminins par excellence, les seins sont aussi le siège du cancer le plus fréquent chez les femmes. Une maladie qui, dans le monde du travail, se heurte parfois à l’invisibilisation de la souffrance.

Emily Dader, 32 ans, a ouvert il y a moins d’un an Trèfle, un restaurant gastronomique 100 % végétal, à Lyon. Son légume estival favori, le poivron, y figure régulièrement au menu.

lemonde.title: La grève au Samusocial de Paris se poursuit, les syndicats dénoncent « la remise à la rue de trop nombreuses familles »

lemonde.title: A Bastia, l’exposition « Corsica-Maghreb » rappelle les allers-retours migratoires entre l’île et l’Afrique du Nord

lemonde.title: Présomption de légitime défense pour les forces de l’ordre : pourquoi la proposition de loi fait débat ?

france24fr.title: Mauritanie : le paradis menacé d’une communauté de pêcheurs
france24fr.description: En Mauritanie, dans le parc national du Banc d’Arguin situé entre le désert et l'océan Altantique, les Imraguens pratiquent une technique de pêche à pied depuis des siècles. Le savoir-faire traditionnel de ce peuple de pêcheurs est menacé par le réchauffement climatique, la surpêche et la difficulté de transmission aux générations futures.

france24fr.title: Istanbul : balade à Balat, quartier coloré où se croisent héritages d’Europe et d’Asie
france24fr.description: Dans le quartier de Balat, sur la rive européenne d’Istanbul, ruelles pavées, maisons aux façades colorées et lieux de culte racontent la ville-monde qu’est Istanbul. Reportage France 2.

france24fr.title: Espagne : un mégafeu ravage plus de 30 000 hectares en Castille
france24fr.description: En Espagne, un mégafeu parti le 16 juillet dans la Sierra Norte de Guadalajara, en Castille-La Manche, a déjà calciné environ 30 à 32 000 hectares. Correspondance de Maude Petit-Jové depuis Madrid pour France 24.

france24fr.title: En Tunisie, les coupures d'électricité se multiplient en pleine canicule
france24fr.description: En Tunisie, une canicule frappe le pays depuis une dizaine de jours. Les températures grimpent et les délestages alimentent la colère. De nombreux Tunisiens dénoncent le manque d'anticipation des autorités.

france24fr.title: Un pub ferme chaque jour au Royaume-Uni, le Premier ministre leur donne un coup de pouce
france24fr.description: Bien décidé à montrer qu'il agit pour améliorer l'économie de son pays et la vie de ses concitoyens, le nouveau Premier ministre britannique, Andy Burnham, a pris jeudi une troisième mesure économique en trois jours, réduisant cette fois-ci la taxe professionnelle des pubs, discothèques et lieux de concert de 20 %.

france24fr.title: Au Cap-vert, le pillage de sable défigure le littoral
france24fr.description: Au Cap-Vert, il ne reste presque plus rien de l’image de carte postale de certaines plages de l’île de Santiago. Pendant des décennies, l’extraction illégale de sable marin pour le secteur du bâtiment a grignoté le littoral. Un trafic qui menace aujourd’hui les écosystèmes, favorise la salinisation des terres agricoles et pousse des femmes à risquer leur santé pour survivre. Récit de Awa Diouf.

france24fr.title: Au Rwanda, lancement de la troisième édition du festival Kigali Ciné Junction
france24fr.description: À Kigali, le rendez-vous désormais bien ancré du cinéma africain a rouvert ses portes. Le festival Kigali Cine Junction offre aux Rwandais cinq jours de projections, d'ateliers et de rencontres, entre écrans en plein air et salle mythique du quartier de Nyamirambo. Correspondance d'Aurore Bayoud pour France 24.

france24fr.title: Au Tchad, 22 000 agents déployés pour évaluer la population du pays
france24fr.description: Le Tchad a lancé le troisième Recensement Général de la Population. Une opération d’ampleur nationale qui n’avait plus été réalisée depuis 2009. L'objectif pour les autorités de Ndjamena est de disposer de données fiables sur une population dont les estimations varient fortement selon les sources. Pour cela plus de 20 000 agents recenseurs ont été déployés à travers le pays. Reportage d'Harold Girard.

france24fr.title: Tunisie : des coupures d'électricité après des températures records
france24fr.description: La tension monte après des coupures d'électricité répétées dans plusieurs régions liées à des opérations de délestage de la Société tunisienne de l'électricité et du gaz. Depuis une dizaine de jours, une canicule frappe le pays avec des températures entre 44 et 49 degrés. Certains tunisiens dénoncent le manque d'anticipation des autorités. Correspondance de Lilia Blaise pour France 24.

france24fr.title: Bulgarie : à 90 ans, un médecin rural toujours au chevet de ses patients
france24fr.description: En Bulgarie, il n'est pas rare de croiser des médecins généralistes qui continuent d'exercer bien au-delà de l'âge de la retraite faute de relève. C'est le cas de Kiril Apostolov : âgé de 90 ans il continue malgré tout d'arpenter les rues de son village pour soigner ses patients. Récit de Marc Paupe.

france24fr.title: Incendies en France : 2 500 hectares partis en fumée dans le sud de la France
france24fr.description: Un incendie d'origine probablement accidentelle, qui a parcouru au moins 2 500 hectares au nord du bassin d'Arcachon et menace des habitations, a conduit à évacuer plus de 20 000 habitants et touristes dans ce secteur de la forêt des Landes de Gascogne, quatre ans après le cauchemar de l'été 2022. Reportage France 2.

france24fr.title: Au Cap-Vert, le pillage de sable met en danger le littoral
france24fr.description: Au Cap-Vert, l'extraction illégale de sable marin pour le secteur du bâtiment grignote le littoral. Sur l'île de Santiago, il ne reste presque plus rien de l'image de carte postale de certaines plages. Des associations dénoncent l'inaction des autorités.

france24fr.title: Violences xénophobes : le Ghana relance l'appel à l'UA sur la situation en Afrique du Sud
france24fr.description: Alors que les attaques xénophobes se poursuivent en Afrique du Sud, le président du Ghana a de nouveau appelé, jeudi, l'Union africaine à débattre de ces violences lors du prochain sommet de l'organisation prévu en février 2027. Plus de 160 000 étrangers ont quitté le pays au cours des deux derniers mois.

france24fr.title: Rwanda : le festival Kigali Ciné Junction ouvre sa 4ème édition
france24fr.description: Au Rwanda, le festival Kigali Ciné Junction ouvre sa 4ème édition. Au menu, cinq jours de projections, d'ateliers et de rencontres. Un rendez-vous entre écran plein air et salles mythiques du quartier de Nyamirambo.

france24fr.title: Cisjordanie : à Sebastia, un site antique menacé réclame la protection de l’Unesco
france24fr.description: Le village de Sebastia espère se voir inscrire à la liste du patrimoine mondial de l’UNESCO, dont l’examen des candidatures se tient jusqu’au 29 juillet. Le site archéologique est menacé par un projet israélien d'expropriation. Il fait l’objet d’une procédure d’urgence, et pourrait aussi figurer sur la liste du patrimoine mondial en péril. Notre correspondante Claire Duhamel s’est rendue sur place.

france24fr.title: Italie : colère après la mort d'un homme interpellé par la police
france24fr.description: La colère gronde en Italie après la mort d'un Marocain plaqué au sol par deux policiers lors d'une arrestation à Bologne, qui provoqué l'indignation d'une partie de l'opinion publique. Décryptage avec Caroline de Camaret, rédactrice en chef du service Europe de France 24.

france24fr.title: Inde : la fronte étudiante continue, Modi promet de punir les fraudeurs
france24fr.description: Le Premier ministre indien Narendra Modi a promis de sanctionner les responsables des fraudes aux examens universitaires à l'origine de la fronde des étudiants, qui continuent en retour d'exiger la démission du ministre de l'Education. Pour en parler, France 24 reçoit sur son plateau Trisha Shetty, militante indienne pour l'égalité entre les genres, fondatrice de "SheSays".

spiegel.title: Nahost: Angriffe der jemenitischen Huthi-Miliz zermürben Israel und USA
spiegel.description: Mit gezielten Nadelstichen zermürbt die jemenitische Huthi-Miliz die militärisch überlegenen Gegner Israel und USA. Das trifft die Weltwirtschaft empfindlich und kam mit Ansage.

spiegel.title: Reise nach Mauretanien, Nigeria, Südafrika: Und dann muss sich Wadephul auch noch zu Spahn äußern
spiegel.description: Außenminister Wadephul besucht drei Staaten Afrikas und trifft auf einen Kontinent der schroffen Gegensätze. Doch dem Regierungsdrama in der Heimat kann auch er kaum entfliehen.

spiegel.title: CDU: Nina Warken soll Kanzleramtschefin werden, Carsten Linnemann das Gesundheitsministerium übernehmen
spiegel.description: Der Kanzler baut seine Regierung um: Gesundheitsministerin Nina Warken soll nach SPIEGEL-Informationen die Lücke im Kanzleramt schließen. Ihr würde wiederum ein weiterer Vertrauter von Friedrich Merz folgen.

spiegel.title: Tour de France 2026: Richard Carapaz siegt, Fragen um Tadej Pogacar
spiegel.description: Der Gesamtführende Tadej Pogačar hat angeblich gesundheitliche Probleme, befeuert werden die Gerüchte durch die Wahl seiner Hose. Richard Carapaz holt sich am Tag vor der Königsetappe den Sieg – am letzten Anstieg.

spiegel.title: »Lori« von Anousch Mueller: Ein atemberaubender Verrat - Kritik
spiegel.description: Ein schrecklicher Bootsunfall, jahrelanges Schweigen: Die Autorin Anousch Müller schildert in »Lori« eine schmerzhafte Reise in die Vergangenheit einer Familie, die ihre Wurzeln in der DDR hat. Ein kunstvolles Buch.

spiegel.title: Karlsruhe: Dienstaufsichtsbeschwerde nach Kothaufen-Vorfall an Grundschule
spiegel.description: Das Klo ist verdreckt. Der Schuldige meldet sich nicht. Was macht der Lehrer? Laut einem Medienbericht lässt er die Jungs mit einem Stück Klopapier ein Stück Stuhlgang aufsammeln und in die Kloschüssel werfen.

spiegel.title: Regensburg: Mögliche Geiselnahme in Bankfiliale – ein Mensch stirbt nach Messerangriff
spiegel.description: Die Polizei ist in Regensburg mit einem Großaufgebot ausgerückt. Ein Mann hat in einer Bankfiliale bei einer mutmaßlichen Geiselnahme einen Menschen tödlich verletzt. Die Bevölkerung soll das Gebiet meiden.

spiegel.title: Indien: 25 Leichen nach Tunnelunglück im Bundesstaat Sikkim geborgen
spiegel.description: Eine verheerende Gasexplosion in Indien hat mehr als zwei Dutzend Menschen das Leben gekostet. Rettungskräfte haben alle Todesopfer aus einem Tunnel geborgen.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: EU-Rekordstrafe für Google, Andy Burnham senkt Gewerbesteuer für Pubs, digitaler Kassenbon
spiegel.description: Der frische britische Premier senkt die Steuern für Pubs. Die EU verhängt eine Rekordstrafe von 890 Millionen Euro gegen Google. Und in Deutschland soll der Kassenbon digital werden. Das ist die Lage am Donnerstagabend.

spiegel.title: Karlsruhe: Bahnmitarbeiter stürzt aus Zug – Staatsanwaltschaft legt Beschwerde ein
spiegel.description: Ein Bahnmitarbeiter stürzte nach einem Gerangel mit einem betrunkenen Fahrgast bei Karlsruhe aus einem fahrenden Zug, das Gericht lehnte einen Haftbefehl gegen den Fahrgast ab. Die Staatsanwaltschaft will das nicht hinnehmen.

spiegel.title: Ali G: Sacha Baron Cohen bringt Kultfigur zurück ins Kino
spiegel.description: Schon in Wimbledon konnte man den Proll mit der gelb getönten Sonnenbrille im Publikum sehen. Jetzt gibt Sacha Baron Cohen bekannt, dass er Ali G wiederbelebt. Und dann ist da noch die Sache mit dem »Tiersex«.

spiegel.title: Wolfsangriff in Italien: »Die Mutter und das Kind haben alles durchs Fenster beobachtet«
spiegel.description: Laut italienischen Fachleuten lief der Wolfsangriff in der Toskana anders ab als zunächst berichtet. Hier erklärt Biologin Ilka Reinhardt, wie Menschen ihre Hunde vor dem Wildtier schützen sollten.

spiegel.title: Brünn in Tschechien: Soldat stirbt bei Helikopterabsturz
spiegel.description: Ein Mensch ist tot, vier weitere sind verletzt: Auf einem Militärflugplatz in Tschechien ist ein Helikopter abgestürzt. Die Unfallursache ist noch unklar.

spiegel.title: Duisburg: Mann stirbt nach Fesselung bei Polizeieinsatz
spiegel.description: Die Staatsanwaltschaft Duisburg ermittelt gegen mehrere Polizisten und Rettungskräfte, weil ein 37-Jähriger nach einem Einsatz gestorben ist. Ein Zusammenhang mit der Fesselung durch die Beamten könne nicht ausgeschlossen werden.

spiegel.title: Ölpreis steigt wieder über 100-Dollar-Marke
spiegel.description: Erst Angriffe in der Straße von Hormus, nun im »Tor der Tränen« vor der Küste des Jemen: Der Irankonflikt eskaliert. Die Weltwirtschaft spürt das schon jetzt. Analysten fürchten, dass der Ölpreis noch höher klettert.

spiegel.title: Ukraine-Krieg: Wer das neue EU-Sanktionspaket gegen Russland verwässerte
spiegel.description: Orbán ist weg, trotzdem ist das 21. EU-Strafpaket gegen Russland abgeschwächt worden. Russischer Fisch bleibt sanktionsfrei, auch Patriarch Kirill muss nichts fürchten. Gleich mehrere Länder bremsten, darunter Deutschland.

spiegel.title: Wisconsin, USA: Polizei erschießt Schwarzen aus nächster Nähe
spiegel.description: Polizisten haben in den USA einen schwarzen Mann bei einem Einsatz erschossen. Videos des Einsatzes lösten bereits Proteste in Madison aus. Nun folgen Ermittlungen.

spiegel.title: Gelsenkirchen: 18-Jährige tarnt Hilferuf bei der Polizei als Pizzabestellung
spiegel.description: Ein Taxifahrer soll eine Frau sexuell belästigt haben. Weil die 18-Jährige Sorge hatte, dass der Mann ihren Notruf mithört, tat sie so, als würde sie eine Pizza bestellen. Die Polizistin am Telefon erkannte die Notlage sofort.

phys-org.title: More than half of Earth's migratory bird species are declining—here's how we can still save them
phys-org.description: Every year, billions of migratory birds connect the world's continents, oceans and ecosystems as they undertake epic journeys between their foraging habitats and breeding grounds.

phys-org.title: Lipid nanoparticles deliver one-two punch to shrink resistant oral tumors in preclinical models
phys-org.description: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is the most common form of head and neck cancer, and the number of new cases is predicted to rise by 30% in the next decade. Despite decades of cancer research, treating OSCC remains a challenge. The five-year survival rate is approximately 50%, and standard treatments such as ablative surgery and radiation often leave patients with permanent disfigurement or profound, lifelong impairment of essential oral functions such as speaking and swallowing.

phys-org.title: Drought, water shortages and crop failures: How does the medieval warm period compare with today?
phys-org.description: A heat wave lasting four months, followed by water shortages and crop failures. This is England in the 13th century, not the 21st. What is often called the Medieval Warm Period saw elevated temperatures in many parts of the world between the 10th and 13th centuries.

phys-org.title: Most powerful Northern Lights in a generation expose weaknesses in UK infrastructure
phys-org.description: Millions of people across the UK marveled at the spectacular northern lights that lit up the night sky in May 2024. But while the display captivated skywatchers, the geomagnetic storm behind it also served as the biggest test in a generation of the UK's preparedness for severe space weather. So did it pass?

phys-org.title: Peptide isolated from a Cerrado frog increases strawberry shelf life
phys-org.description: Five minutes. That was the amount of time that Oso Grande strawberries remained in contact with the Ctx(Ile21)-Ha peptide—a molecule isolated from a frog native to the Brazilian Cerrado—in experiments conducted in Brazil by scientists at the Tupã campus of São Paulo State University (UNESP). It was enough to demonstrate the molecule's potential to extend the shelf life of the fruit, which is highly perishable.

phys-org.title: Chasing subseasonal forecasts with AI
phys-org.description: Subseasonal forecasting, or the ability to predict weather trends two weeks to two months in advance, is a capability highly sought after in various economic sectors, including energy, water management and agriculture. Reliable forecasts on this scale have thus far been largely out of reach, but researchers at the U.S. National Science Foundation National Center for Atmospheric Research (NSF NCAR) are leveraging AI to see whether it can help them grasp this elusive capability.

phys-org.title: Would you trust AI for ethical advice?

phys-org.title: Moon baboon: New insight into the mind of ancient Egyptians

phys-org.title: From one frontier to another: The quantum revolution
phys-org.description: Manchester's quantum researchers are building on the Ferranti Mark I legacy, using ultra-pure silicon and single atoms to move quantum computing closer to real-world impact.

phys-org.title: How much should you reveal about yourself on your dating profile? Scientists have found the 'sweet spot'

On dating apps, the way people present themselves through their profiles can significantly influence how approachable, trustworthy and likable they appear.

phys-org.title: Researchers find college-educated population more likely to shelter during dangerous wildfire smoke
phys-org.description: American adults with college degrees now outlive those without degrees by more than eight years, in part because graduates appear to be more proactive about protecting their health. For example, they smoke cigarettes at far lower rates and follow cancer screening advice more often, especially after a relative is diagnosed. Even as studies documented such disparities, the health gap widened.

phys-org.title: Shaking atoms to bring black-hole quantum chaos into the lab
phys-org.description: Physicists have discovered a surprisingly simple way to reproduce one of the most fascinating models in modern physics—linked to black holes, quantum chaos and exotic electronic materials—using ultracold atoms trapped in light.

phys-org.title: Molecular clock transitions tune out the noise in the hunt for new physics
phys-org.description: Heavy polar molecules are some of the most sensitive tools physicists have for probing what lies beyond the Standard Model, the theory that describes the particles and forces we know about. But turning that sensitivity into precise, trustworthy measurements has long been held back by one stubborn problem: Stray electric and magnetic fields drown out the tiny signals researchers are actually looking for.

phys-org.title: Predicting where wildfire smoke will go next
phys-org.description: In recent summers, wildfire smoke has been inescapable across Wisconsin, drifting south from Canada and leading to long stretches of poor air quality. Whether that smoke clears or lingers is often influenced in part by the atmospheric boundary layer—the lowest part of the atmosphere, where airborne particles mix and move.

phys-org.title: Fig-leaf enzyme turns tannery waste into high-value collagen
phys-org.description: Tanneries generate large quantities of skin trimmings before hides are tanned. These trimmings contain collagen but are commonly treated as low-value waste. An international research team has developed a method that uses ficin, a protein-digesting enzyme obtained from fig leaves, to recover type I collagen from lambskin trimming waste.

phys-org.title: Older teens entering care often overlooked
phys-org.description: There is an urgent need for better support for older teenagers entering care for the first time, new Griffith University research has found. Professor Silke Meyer from Griffith's School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work conducted a scoping review that examined research on older adolescents ages 15–17.

phys-org.title: No perfect job? Moving forward despite uncertainty may make work more meaningful
phys-org.description: People who accept that there may not always be a perfect career choice and learn to make decisions despite uncertainty are more likely to find their work meaningful, satisfying and engaging, according to research published in the Journal of Counseling Psychology.

phys-org.title: New teaching method could help Aboriginal languages survive and thrive
phys-org.description: Curtin University-led research has unveiled a new teaching approach that could help incorporate Aboriginal languages into Australian classrooms, teach younger generations and potentially prevent important cultural connections from being lost.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?

But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

proj-syn.title: Yes, the Hong Kong of Old Is Over
proj-syn.description: The pro-China camp continues to tout Hong Kong’s resilience, recently pointing to the fact that the city has reclaimed its position as the global IPO leader. But conveniently left out of this narrative is that resilience has come to depend on the direct intervention of the Chinese authorities.

proj-syn.title: Why Iran Won’t Change
proj-syn.description: Embedded in the Islamic Republic’s foundations is a doctrine that allows for total repression of the population and mobilization of all state resources to preserve the system. This helps to explain why the US and Israel were wrong to expect the regime to change its behavior, let alone be brought down by the Iranian people.

proj-syn.title: Rethinking Global Imbalances
proj-syn.description: Today’s global imbalances, starting with China's massive trade surplus, are not simply the result of poor macroeconomic coordination. Rather, they reflect long-term strategic thinking and a departure from the bias toward openness on which the postwar trade order was built.

proj-syn.title: What the New UK Chancellor Means for the UK Economy
proj-syn.description: By appointing John Healey as chancellor of the exchequer, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has taken a calculated risk. If Healey can leverage his insider knowledge of the Treasury, pursue a bold, pro-growth agenda, and manage his defense-spending instincts, he may be able to provide the structural shake-up the UK economy needs.

proj-syn.title: Will the US Climate War with Canada Become Global?
proj-syn.description: For the first time, a great power has moved to price transboundary climate-driven harms–massive wildfires–and extract compensation unilaterally. What was previously a development, insurance, or emissions-accounting issue is now a security and trade dispute between two G7 economies, setting a precedent that others may try to follow.

proj-syn.title: America Is Closing the Door on Opportunity—and Talent
proj-syn.description: Viewed in isolation, the Trump administration's new, more restrictive student-visa policy may seem modest. But as part of a broader retreat from openness, it signals that the country once known for offering ambitious outsiders a chance to transform their lives is less willing to do so.

proj-syn.title: Large Language Models for Small Language Communities
proj-syn.description: Many developing economies cannot access large language models, most of which have been trained on datasets in English. To build scalable and inclusive LLMs for countries with minority languages, policymakers' best bet is to tap mobile network operators, with their armies of developers and data-processing capabilities.

proj-syn.title: The Epstein Class Was Made Offshore
proj-syn.description: The impunity of Jeffrey Epstein and his associates is the predictable upshot of unbridled wealth concentration, facilitated by the offshore financial system. In fact, that system represents the selective withdrawal by a privileged few from the rule of law, without the loss of any of its benefits.

proj-syn.title: A New Tool for Combating Human Trafficking
proj-syn.description: While human trafficking is mostly framed as a macro phenomenon, this does not fully explain how these criminal networks operate. Recognizing that trafficking corridors link specific source and destination localities offers a stronger basis for policy than a purely national approach or isolated interventions.

proj-syn.title: The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly in Global Tax Negotiations
proj-syn.description: Ongoing negotiations at the United Nations offer the international community the best chance that it will have to ensure that global taxation authority is assigned fairly. With multinationals and the ultra-rich abusing the current system to minimize their tax payments, finalizing a new convention is an urgent priority.

proj-syn.title: The Bayer Truth About Trump’s Farm and Food Policies
proj-syn.description: A new executive order on regenerative agriculture might seem to suggest that US President Donald Trump’s administration wants to help American farmers. But a closer look at the order and other recent developments reveals a familiar pattern: an unhappy public gets reassuring words, while corporate interests receive tangible support.

proj-syn.title: Don’t Overestimate America and China’s Importance
proj-syn.description: Some commentators on international affairs seem to think that “the West” and the BRICS+ do not really matter; only the United States and China do. Yet three factors complicate this simplistic framing, suggesting that even superpowers' influence has limits, and that smaller powers can sometimes punch above their weight.

proj-syn.title: Colombia’s Rightward Turn
proj-syn.description: There is a growing tension in Colombia between the popular demand for a strong welfare state and a political system that cannot deliver on that promise unless it breaks free from malign influences. Since the incoming administration is aligned with many of those interests, Colombians will continue to be disappointed.

proj-syn.title: A Cold War Adventure in Portugal
proj-syn.description: Just 52 years after escaping military dictatorship, Portugal is an EU and eurozone member and the world’s seventh-safest country. While Donald Trump's systematic destruction of the rules-based global order will not reverse this progress, nor will it do any good for Portugal, the US, or anyone else.

proj-syn.title: Social-Media Age Bans Won’t Make Children Safer—But This Will
proj-syn.description: As the European Union considers how to protect and empower young people in a digital world, it must resist the urge only to enact a ban on social media for young people. A more effective strategy would force tech companies to remove addictive features by holding them to product-liability standards—as with most other industries.

proj-syn.title: Who Will Sit Atop the Next World Order?
proj-syn.description: American hegemony has given way to a global order based on rivalry and competition among several major powers, where there is no longer a fixed, codified set of rules. Instead, there is only economic, technological, and military power—the likes of which China is amassing faster than many observers realize.

proj-syn.title: AI Will Supercharge Surveillance Capitalism
proj-syn.description: For too long, governments have stood by and allowed the creation of business models built on the commercial exploitation of users' personal data and that reward social and psychological manipulation. With the AI industry poised to replicate this model, policymakers must intervene before it is too late.
